clue.text: Air traveller, the fool, is blocking someone from Estonia?

indicators.note: to block is to sit in the way, so these letters sit inside the Estonian's word

parts.note: a Balt is a native of one of the Baltic states, Estonia among them
a loon is a crazy or foolish person

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at a foolish sky traveller who seems to be getting in an Estonian's way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rides in a hot-air craft is a traveller through the air.

clue.text: Prevent Light Infantry interrupting someone working in ammunition supply

parts.note: to ban something is to prevent it

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so these letters go inside the worker

parts.note: a doer is someone who gets things done, a worker
LI is the military abbreviation for Light Infantry

explanation.surface: Soldiers barging into a munitions worker's job, stopping supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder belt with loops for cartridges is a way of carrying and supplying ammunition.

clue.text: Topped smooth vegetable

indicators.note: topped means having its top cut off; in a down entry the top is the first letter

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: A vegetable with its top trimmed, looking smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh national emblem, it is an allium grown as a vegetable.

clue.text: Disallowed assessment of racecourse without reserve

parts.note: something ruled out is not allowed
in horse racing the going is the official description of the ground's condition

explanation.surface: A racing official rules out a ground report and acts without holding anything back.
explanation.walkthrough: The GOING is a British racing term: the state of the turf, such as good or soft, announced before a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociable, friendly person shows no reserve or shyness.

clue.text: No bad feeling after abandoning one aristocrat

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving something behind, so the word for one is taken out

parts.note: bile means bitterness or ill temper
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with no hard feelings, having given someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the titled class, the nobility.

clue.text: Street in good condition showing no extreme shady activity?

indicators.note: having no extreme means one end letter is dropped, here the last

parts.note: to be in good health is to be in good condition

explanation.surface: A street in fine shape with nothing extreme about it, yet something shady going on.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: acting by stealth means working in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret, furtive action is a kind of underhand behaviour done out of sight.

clue.text: Book club in Calais arranged time for special project

indicators.note: in places these letters within the rearranged town
arranged means set out in a new order

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games such as cricket

explanation.surface: A book club meeting in Calais organises time away for a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calais' is not a place here: 'arranged' reshuffles the town's six letters so that they wrap around the book and club.
explanation.definitionFit: Academics take leave from normal duties for a period of research or study.

clue.text: Vegetable casserole: not entirely a small amount

parts.note: a casserole is cooked in a pot

indicators.note: not entirely means a word with its final letter missing

parts.note: a tot is a small measure, as of spirits

explanation.surface: A vegetable casserole that does not quite make up a full small portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber such as a spud is a staple vegetable.

clue.text: Activity with sailors and soldiers — head of troops gets decoration

parts.note: ado is fuss or bustle, activity
RN is the Royal Navy
men is a usual crossword word for soldiers, the rank and file

indicators.note: the head is the front, so only the leading letter is taken

explanation.surface: Military busyness with navy and army, and the officer leading the troops gets a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament or embellishment is something added as a decoration.

clue.text: Time engaged in booze — very much turning purple

indicators.note: engaged in means placed within, so the time letter goes inside

parts.note: beer is booze

indicators.note: turning means the word for very much is read backwards

parts.note: too means excessively, very much

explanation.surface: Drinking too long, someone's face is going purple.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep red-violet colour of a root vegetable is used to describe a flushed face.

clue.text: Signal to do time?

definitions.meaning: a light or fire warning or guiding people is a signal
read as three words, ..., meaning serve a prison sentence as a convict

explanation.surface: A signal that it is time to act.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BE A CON: to be a convict is to do time in prison; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning fire or lighthouse light serves as a signal.

clue.text: The French brought in lettuce required by regulation salad

indicators.note: brought in places the French word inside the lettuce

parts.note: cos is a variety of lettuce
le is French for the
a law is a regulation

explanation.surface: French rules demanding lettuce in a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded cabbage with mayonnaise is a common side salad.

clue.text: Source of downpour possibly making the car and ultimately you wet

indicators.note: possibly shows the letters could be in another order
ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A downpour might drench the car and, in the end, you too.
explanation.definitionFit: A water slide at a pool sends a rush of water down with the rider, a playful source of a soaking.

clue.text: Certain latitude, too much in Parisian style, reduced formality

parts.note: trop is French for too much

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing a last letter

parts.note: ice means coldness or stiff reserve in manner

explanation.surface: A sophisticated French-style relaxation of manners, at a particular latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer and Capricorn are the two lines of latitude bounding the tropics.

clue.text: Responds sharply, with passion, seeing paparazzo's aim

parts.note: to snap is to retort sharply
hot means passionate

explanation.surface: A celebrity snaps back angrily, which is just what the photographer wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick informal photograph is what a celebrity photographer hopes to capture.

clue.text: Anger about private secretary leading a king to deliver: "Twerp!"

indicators.note: leading means coming in front of what follows
about means around, so the anger word goes round the secretary

parts.note: pique is resentment or irritation
PS is the abbreviation for private secretary
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A furious aide shoves the king to deliver an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A small insignificant person is called by this dismissive word for a nobody.

clue.text: Dad's transaction will secure billions, OK?

parts.note: pa is dad, with the s from the possessive

indicators.note: to secure is to hold safe within, so the sale goes round the billions

parts.note: a sale is a transaction

explanation.surface: Asking whether a father's huge business deal is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate or acceptable describes something that will do, merely all right.

clue.text: Chef regularly cooked almost all rice and veg

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is used
cooked shows letters mixed up
almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A chef cooking nearly all the rice plus some vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives CE from Chef; 'almost' cuts ALL to AL; 'cooked' turns AL plus RICE into LERIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A knobbly root related to celery is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Greasy river offering unexciting work, nothing more

parts.note: limp means lacking energy, feeble
op is short for opus, a work
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An oily river offering only dull work.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Just So Stories describe 'the great grey-green, greasy Limpopo River' in southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Kipling description of an African waterway calls it greasy, so the adjective points to it.

clue.text: Turn up program that's getting attention

parts.note: an app is a computer program
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A program arrives that is attracting attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up or arrive is to come into view.

clue.text: Girl rested in middle of week

indicators.note: in places the resting word between the middle letters
middle of takes the central letters, the double E

parts.note: lain is the past participle of lie, rested

explanation.surface: A girl took a rest in the middle of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in the Arthurian maid of Astolat.

clue.text: Source of light unable to function, needing some current quietly introduced

indicators.note: introduced means put inside

parts.note: lost means helpless, unable to cope
an amp is a unit of electric current
p is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A broken light needing some electricity put in quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A street light on a post is a source of light.

clue.text: Pointless climbing — without this?

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means read from bottom to top

parts.note: pointless split as no tip, having no point

explanation.surface: Climbing is pointless without this piece of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns NOTIP upwards; the whole clue also says climbing would be pointless without one.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal spike hammered into rock is a climber's essential anchor.

clue.text: See 26
Something observed by many Italians in Vietnam

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the word

explanation.surface: Something many Italians watch in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is visible to many people across Sicily.

clue.text: See 9
Vegetable spread served with crackers and Scotch

parts.note: butter is a spread
crackers means crazy, nuts
to scotch a rumour is to quash it

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish with butter, crackers and whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear-shaped winter gourd is cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: Buffoon displaying energy between two hills

indicators.note: between places the energy letter in the gap separating the two hill words

parts.note: a mount and a bank are both hills
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A clown showing energy between two hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan or clownish performer selling quack remedies is a show-off fool.
